subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC/on-prem network qualification - Acme
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC/on-prem network qualification - Acme

Hi Michael,

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap of what we discussed and the action items so we have alignment before the technical deep dive: 

Summary of high-level performance targets (agreed on call):
- P95 end-to-end latency target: < 150 ms for 512-token responses (user request -> first token).
- Token streaming requirement: token-level streaming with < 50 ms inter-token latency for interactive flows.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline sustained concurrency target 400 concurrent sessions, peak bursts up to ~1,000 for short periods. Estimated steady-state tokens/sec workload: ~25k TPS during peak.
- Availability and fallbacks: primary route via VPC peering; fallback via site-to-site VPN if peering is not feasible.

Network / private deployment considerations we flagged on the call:
- Preferred connectivity: Direct VPC Peering (AWS) in us-west-2. If peering not possible, managed site-to-site VPN (IPSec) as fallback.
- Egress: Acme currently routes egress through NAT Gateways. We need to confirm whether static egress IPs are required for your firewall rules.
- Ports/protocols: HTTPS (443) required outbound from your inference callers to Redwood endpoints.
- MTU and path MTU: recommend 1500; if you're using Jumbo frames on-prem, please confirm so we can validate fragment behavior for streaming.
- Internal latency budget expectations (example): app -> LB: 5 ms, LB -> inference node: 10 ms, inference runtime processing: 80-120 ms depending on model/sequence, return path + client rendering budget to keep p95 under 150 ms.

Requested artifacts / next steps (action items):
1) Acme: share a traceroute / mtr from your app hosts to the candidate peering subnet and any NAT egress IPs (attachment stub accepted).
2) Acme: confirm whether static egress IPs can be assigned or whether traffic will come from variable NAT ranges.
3) Redwood (Marissa & Aditya): validate expected runtime latency under the workload profile and propose any batching/quantization tradeoffs to meet the p95 target.
4) Schedule a technical sync (30-45 minutes) with your network engineering team to review topology, firewall rules, and test windows.

Attachments: redwood-slo-network-checklist.pdf (network checklist & sample firewall rules).

Proposed times for tech call: Thu Apr 5 09:00-11:00 PT or Fri Apr 6 13:00-15:00 PT. Tell me what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
Jordan Blake | Redwood Inference

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Network Team <network@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 13:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC/on-prem network qualification - Acme

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from the network side: 

- Our environment: Acme runs in AWS us-west-2 with private subnets behind NAT Gateways. We can set up VPC peering to Redwood if you provide the peer CIDR and recommended route table changes.
- Static egress IPs: currently egress is via auto-scaling NAT Gateways, so IPs are not fixed. We can stand up an Elastic IP / dedicated NAT Gateway for the test window if static egress is required for firewall whitelisting.
- Ports: we only need to allow outbound TCP/443. We do have strict egress filtering, so static egress would simplify things.
- Traceroute: attached is acme-traceroute-20280403.txt from our app host to your candidate endpoint (stub). Looks like there are 3 hops inside our VPC before hitting the internet NAT.
- VPN vs Peering: prefer peering for performance; VPN as fallback if peering is blocked by our security review.

Proposed test window: Mon Apr 9 08:00-10:00 PT to run latency and streaming tests. If you (Redwood) can provision a test endpoint and provide load script details, we'll run from a small fleet of representative app hosts.

CCing network@acme.com so they have the details.

-Michael
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

--

Michael, can you confirm the Mon Apr 9 08:00-10:00 PT window and whether you can provision a temporary dedicated NAT (Elastic IP) for the test? If not, we'll work with peering + security group rules and try to arrange deterministic egress via our test harness.
